passage:
Thursday: Zubin, five, peers at Chachi's baby asleep in the cradle. 'Why doesn't she have a name yet?' Dadi says, 'On Sunday everyone will come and give it to her.'
Sunday: Forty people squeeze into the flat. The pandit whispers into the baby's ear, and Chacha announces, 'Sharmila!' Everyone claps. Zubin tries to count the guests and gives up.
Monday: Zubin asks Mumma, 'Why did so many people come for one tiny baby?' Mumma says, 'Because she belongs to all of us now. Like you do.' Zubin leans over the cradle. 'Hi, Sharmila. I'm yours too.'

qa.q: What was Zubin feeling when he asked why so many people came?
qa.a: He felt curious and a little amazed, puzzled that one tiny baby could bring so many people together.

qa.q: What did Mumma's answer give Zubin?
qa.a: A simple reason he could understand, that a baby belongs to the whole family, which helped him feel part of the welcome too.

qa.q: What would it mean for baby Sharmila to grow up with so many people at her naming?
qa.a: She would grow up knowing a big circle of family counts her as their own, just as Mumma said.

grounding: Shows a young child who watches a baby cousin's naming ceremony, asks why so many people came, and learns that a new life belongs to a wide family circle.

passage: It poured all morning on the day of baby Aamir's aqiqah, and the tent on the terrace leaked. Still people kept arriving, dripping: Khalas, Mamus, neighbours, even Jeevan Uncle from downstairs holding his umbrella over two old aunties. Asif, six, watched Chachu gently shave the baby's fuzzy hair while Dadi murmured a prayer. Aamir cried; everyone laughed kindly. Asif tugged Ammi's sleeve. 'Why did all these people come in the rain for a baby who just cries?' Ammi smiled. 'Because now he's everyone's Aamir. Same as you were.' Asif looked at the wet crowd again and stood a little taller.

qa.q: Who held an umbrella over two old aunties?
How did Asif feel after Ammi's answer, and what shows it?
qa.a: He felt proud and included, standing a little taller as he realised he too belongs to that wide circle.

qa.q: How did Ammi help Asif understand the ceremony?
qa.a: She answered his honest question simply and linked it to his own babyhood, so he could see what the gathering meant.

qa.q: What does Jeevan Uncle coming in the rain suggest about how the neighbours see the baby?
qa.a: It suggests the neighbours feel part of the family's joy, willing to brave the rain to welcome Aamir.

grounding: Illustrates a young child at a baby cousin's first-haircut and naming rite who asks why so many came, and learns that a life belongs to a wider circle of family, faith and neighbours.
